# RESULTS_BY_COMPARISON.md -- one table per research variable

*Generated by `.wrapup/mktables.py` from `experiments.sqlite` (read-only).  Do not hand-edit; rerun the generator.*

**Shape rules.** column 1 = everything held constant, column 2 = the varied variable, the remaining columns = one per benchmark.  Columns are never filtered (an empty benchmark column still appears).  A row with no benchmark value at all is dropped; a column-1 group with fewer than 2 values of the varied variable is dropped (nothing to compare); nothing else is ever dropped.

**x-axis.** quantisation is always plotted against EFFECTIVE BPW = 8 x file_bytes / n_params from `.wrapup/bpw_map.json`.  Nominal labels such as `Q2`/`Q3` are never used: they span 2.76-5.04 bpw.

**Cells.** `score (n)` -- the number in parentheses is `n_items`, so an item-level SE is `sqrt(p(1-p)/n)`.  `-` = not measured (no row in the DB); the report never substitutes 0.0 for a missing cell.  Every table's top row reports rows shown and columns with data.

**Columns.** HumanEval / HumanEval+ / MBPP / MBPP+ = EvalPlus 0.3.1 on the full problem set (164/164/378/378), greedy chat. MultiPL-E = retired panel pooled over its languages (cpp/python/java/js/rs/rb, 155-161 items each), raw greedy, canonical protocol only.  MMLU / ARC-c / TruthfulQA = lm-eval 0.4.13 loglikelihood shim; GSM8K / IFEval = lm-eval 0.4.13 greedy chat; all with server-side thinking off.

**One variable per table.** Panel-tagged recipes (`mNN-...`, e.g. the m55 expert-wise files) change something other than raw bpw, so they are kept out of tables A/B/C and appear only in their own table (D).  That keeps each table varying exactly one thing.
